dedupe_keys.name: open database on global coal and metal mine production

description: This open database covers global extraction of coal and metal ores at the level of individual mines: 1,171 mines in 80 countries with mine-level production of 80 materials from 2000 to 2021. It was compiled by Simon Jasansky, Mirko Lieber, Stefan Giljum and Victor Maus to give open, source-linked mine data for environmental and economic research, and is described in a Data Descriptor in Scientific Data (2023). Besides production it holds mine coordinates, ownership, mineral reserves, mining waste, transport of mining products, and the capacity and output of smelters and refineries, in 12 linked tables gathered by hand from more than 1,900 public sources such as company annual and sustainability reports, each data point linked to its source; mines without coordinates are linked to GADM administrative units. Version 1.0.3 is a free 1.1 MB zip download under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: coverage is limited to companies that publish reports, so small, state and artisanal mines are under-represented, and coordinates were partly geocoded. For simulation it supports supply-chain, hazard exposure and capacity planning studies of mineral supply down to single mines and processing plants. Related catalogue records include the global mining polygons of Maus et al., the Global Coal Mine Tracker and the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries.
